title: Satya Prakash Gupta v. State of U.P. and Others
court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
coram: Manoj Kumar Gupta and Manish Kumar Nigam, JJ.
disposition: Writ disposed; dues dispute relegated to clause 6.5.
headnote: A dispute over the correctness of electricity dues, including whether the consumer consumed energy, cannot be decided in writ. The petition was disposed of, leaving the petitioner to object before respondent No. 3 for a decision under clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 within four weeks of receipt of the objection.
facts: The petitioner, Satya Prakash Gupta, challenged successive bills by which the Electricity Department demanded electricity dues. The connection had earlier stood in his father's name and had been disconnected. On payment of Rs. 20,000 towards those dues, the Department restored the connection, while the balance remained unpaid. The petitioner said he had not consumed electricity for a long period and that the demand was incorrect. The Department's case was that restoration followed only a part payment of the outstanding amount.

holding_units.topic: Disputed electricity dues left to a clause 6.5 objection
holding_units.holding: The dispute over the amount demanded by the electricity bills cannot be decided in writ jurisdiction. The petitioner may place his objection before respondent No. 3, which is to be decided under clause 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005 within four weeks of receipt of the objection. The writ petition is disposed of on that basis.

principle_tags.application: The High Court declined to decide in writ whether the petitioner had consumed electricity and whether the Department's dues were correct, and disposed of the petition so that the objection could be decided under clause 6.5.
The course left open against the impugned demand was an objection to respondent No. 3, to be decided under clause 6.5 within four weeks of its receipt.

not_decided.point: Whether the petitioner consumed electricity and whether the balance demanded after the part payment of Rs. 20,000 is correct
not_decided.note: Left to respondent No. 3 on an objection under clause 6.5
